failure_summary.description: Ready requests were ignored, refined with a fresh search instead of the compatible cached result, or applied to the wrong target or domain.
A user-supplied category or code was changed or misread, or a filter received an argument belonging to another domain.
Plans omitted required calls or result saves, or imported unavailable tool modules instead of using the runtime-provided functions.

patch.reasoning: The skill already specifies cache refinement, direct runtime tool use, and result saving, so repeating those rules would not address the gap. These edits clarify two recurring interpretation failures: affirmations to questions about a specific domain or type create an actionable request, and categorical values should not be silently normalized or mapped to a different preference slot.

edits.target: Resolve elliptical latest turns against the immediately preceding assistant question and all still-pending user requests before deciding what action is needed.
edits.content: When the assistant asks whether the user wants to explore a named supported domain or category, an affirmative reply makes that specific search pending even if the domain was not previously active; carry the named domain, target, or type into the appropriate search.

edits.target: ## Validate tool arguments and preserve user intent
edits.content: - Preserve user-supplied category, cuisine, airline-code, and other categorical values when passing them to compatible string or list fields; do not silently substitute a nearby example label or synonym. Resolve terse replies using the assistant’s immediately preceding question to select the argument slot, and normalize a value only when the schema explicitly requires a canonical enum value.
